title: Chinon and the Loire
subtitle: Cabernet Franc on its own
objectives: Describe the Loire's Cabernet Franc appellations

steps.title: The appellations
steps.body: In the Loire's Touraine and Anjou-Saumur, Cabernet Franc makes most of the red wine. Chinon, Bourgueil and Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil, in Touraine, and Saumur-Champigny, in Saumur, are the key appellations. The wines are medium-bodied, fresh and perfumed, with raspberry, violet and graphite.

steps.title: Soil matters
steps.body: Soils shape the style. Sandy and gravel soils near the rivers give light, fruity wines to drink young. Tuffeau, a soft, white limestone, and clay-limestone on the slopes give more structured wines that can age 10 to 20 years. The same tuffeau was used to build the Loire's châteaux.

steps.prompt: Which soil in Chinon gives the most structured, age-worthy Cabernet Franc?
steps.explanation: Limestone slopes give firmer, longer-lived wines than riverside sand and gravel.

steps.title: Styles
steps.body: Loire Cabernet Franc ranges from light, juicy wines, served cool in Paris bistros, to serious, oaked wines from old vines. Rosé de Loire and Cabernet d'Anjou, a rosé often off-dry, also use it. Cooler vintages can show more green notes; warmer ones, riper fruit.

steps.prompt: Which are Loire Cabernet Franc appellations?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Chinon, Bourgueil and Saumur-Champigny are key appellations
Gravel gives light wines; tuffeau gives structured ones
Styles range from bistro reds to age-worthy wines
